quotes.text: A well phrased request to Copilot can strip an hour long grind down to a few focused minutes for email meetings or document prep.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the core productivity promise of good prompting in one sentence.

quotes.text: One simple but powerful prompt I often suggest is this list the five key decisions, five action items with owners and outstanding risks from the meeting.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a concrete, reusable meeting prompt.

quotes.text: If you ask for patterns or anomalies, it doesn't just build a chart. It interprets the results with context. That's the meaningful difference.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why Copilot in Excel goes beyond formula help.

quotes.text: A one off prompt gives you something nice and quick. Chaining those prompts across your Microsoft three sixty five workflow builds something bigger, the kind of productivity rhythm where you stay focused on the work instead of the navigation.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the shift from isolated prompts to connected workflows.

quotes.text: Pick your single biggest daily roadblock, frame it into a simple prompt, and run it through Copilot tomorrow. Watch the difference when it clears the path.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear, actionable next step for listeners.

Turning email chaos into a five-minute task
From spreadsheet wrestling to instant insights
Measuring when Copilot has paid for itself

takeaways: Copilot's ROI comes from plugging the small daily leaks of email triage, meeting follow-ups and spreadsheet preparation.
Specific prompts that ask for decisions, owners, risks or patterns turn raw emails, meetings and data into outcomes you can act on.
Chaining prompts across Excel, Word, Outlook and Teams removes context switches and compounds the value beyond minutes saved.
hook: Most Microsoft 365 Copilot users barely scratch its potential and lose hours to inbox triage, meeting notes and spreadsheet wrestling. In this episode Mirko Peters shares the prompts he uses every day, for knowledge workers and managers who want Copilot to pay for its license and turn routine work into clear outcomes.
